## SCE Extends Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program Claim Submission Deadline to Dec. 31


One-time extension comes as interest remains high, giving community members additional time to consider their recovery options from the Eaton Fire.


November 24, 2026


****[Media Relations:](https://newsroom.edison.com/) 626-302-2255,[\[email protected\]](https://newsroom.edison.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#69070c1e1a291a0a0c470a0604)
[Investor Relations:](https://www.edison.com/home/investors.html) Sam Ramraj, 626-302-2540
Feinberg/Biros: Amy Weiss, 202-203-0448,[\[email protected\]](https://newsroom.edison.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#f8999581b88f9d918b8b888d9a94919b999e9e99918a8bd69b9795)


ROSEMEAD, Calif., Nov. 24, 2026 — In response to requests for more time from community members and leaders, Southern California Edison today announced a one-time extension of the[Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program](https://sce.com/directclaims) claim submission deadline to Dec. 31, 2026. The extension comes as claim submissions continue at their highest levels of 2026 and reflects the company’s continued commitment to the community’s recovery.


“Community members and leaders have told us there continues to be strong interest in the program and a need for more time to participate,” said[Pedro J. Pizarro](https://energized.edison.com/wildfire-recovery-compensation-program#deadline) , president and CEO of Edison International, SCE’s parent company. “Eligible community members who submit a claim by December 31 can learn what compensation is available through the program and then decide whether it is right for them.”


**The Deadline is to Submit, Not Finish**


Dec. 31 is the deadline to submit a claim, not the deadline to receive or accept an offer. For those uncertain about whether the program is right for them, submitting a claim by year-end keeps that option available while they decide. It also preserves their opportunity to receive and evaluate an offer after the submission deadline.


- It takes about two hours to submit a claim. Submitting a claim, receiving an offer and evaluating that offer do not waive a claimant’s rights, including the option to pursue litigation.
- Offers are being delivered in about 36 days on average once claims are substantially complete.
- Payments are made within 30 days after settlement conditions are satisfied, with many payments occurring within two to three weeks.


For those who believe compensation through litigation may be available soon because the first bellwether trial begins in March, the trial involves only eight households selected by the court. It does not mean these households and others will receive compensation shortly afterward. Traditional litigation can take years, with some claims from wildfires in 2017 and 2018 still pending. Through the SCE program, community members can receive fair offers and payments in a fraction of that time.


**Interest in the Program Continues to Grow**


The Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program provides compensation in line with previous wildfire settlements through a more streamlined process with less paperwork and a shorter path to resolution. As of Nov. 24, 2026:


- More than 6,300 claims submitted, consisting of over 19,000 individuals, trusts and legal entities, with 43% submitted by attorneys or authorized representatives.
- More than 3,500 offers extended to over 8,700 claimants, totaling about $1.2 billion. More than 80% of offers have been accepted, with more pending. Only about 2% of offers have been declined.
- Nearly 5,000 claimants paid, totaling $700 million, with many more in process.


Since the program launched in October 2025, SCE has held nearly two dozen community meetings and pop-up events. Additional engagement opportunities will be offered in December to answer questions and provide support with submitting claims by the Dec. 31 deadline.


- One-on-one assistance, in-person appointments and walk-in support are available for people who need help understanding the program or completing a claim. Call 888-912-8528 to get started.
- To submit a claim and access detailed guidance in English and Spanish, visit the[Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program web page](https://www.sce.com/directclaims) .


**About Southern California Edison**


An Edison International (NYSE: EIX) company, Southern California Edison is one of the nation’s largest electric utilities, serving a population of approximately 15 million via 5 million customer accounts in a 50,000-square-mile service area within Central, Coastal and Southern California.
